title: Victorian election 2026 live: voters head to the polls as Coalition seeks to topple Labor – latest news
description:
Follow live updates today and results tonight as Labor’s Ben Carroll and Liberal leader Jess Wilson seek victory in Victoria’s state election

text: Treaty at stake at this election

Both the Coalition led by Jess Wilson and One Nation have pledged to repeal Victoria’s treaty with First Nations people if they win the election. The treaty established the Gellung Warl, a representative body for Indigenous people which has the power to make rules on a limited number of matters directly affecting First Nations peoples. It does not have the power to veto policy or legislation.
A Parliamentary Budget Office report requested by Wilson earlier this year found that repealing the treaty laws would save taxpayers $948.3m over the next 10 years. Labor disputed the figures.
Just under two hours til polls close

We are less than two hours away from polls closing. The ABC reported there was a late rush at the polling booth at Melbourne town hall, so it seems a few people who were a bit wary of the rain earlier are heading out now.

Our live stream will kick off an hour after polls close at 7pm AEDT, with Barrie Cassidy, Matilda Boseley, and Benita Kolovos bringing you all the news, plus we will have reporters at the Liberal, Labor and Greens election night parties as the results come in.
You can view the live stream on the Guardian website, YouTube or Instagram.
Hanson meets Santa while campaigning
Pauline Hanson has drawn crowds on election day in Victoria, AAP reports.
One Nation’s campaign bus headed to polling booths east of Melbourne on Saturday morning, after touring electorates in the city’s north the previous day.
In Koo Wee Rup, local candidate Nikole Schellekens was happy ceding the floor to Hanson, offering to take photos for supporters keen to get their picture taken with the party leader.
Amid the fanfare, a man dressed as Santa Claus made an appearance, telling onlookers Hanson had “been a very good girl this year” before embracing her.
While Hanson received a mostly warm reception in the electorates of Pakenham, Narracan and Bass, she did meet some opposition at a polling booth in Frankston.
One heckler told her “we do not want racist, Trump-style politics in Victoria” while a group of Labor volunteers shouted “put One Nation last” as she walked by.
One Nation’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, told reporters:
double quotation markIf it’s not us that forms government, we will hold whoever does form government’s feet to the fire. But … we will also work with anyone to achieve better outcomes for Victoria.
Second polling booth closes due to weather
The Victorian Electoral Commission has announced the polling booth at Saints Peter and Paul Serbian Orthodox Church Hall in Wodonga has shut due to the weather conditions.
This follows Keysborough Gardens primary school shutting earlier due to flooding.
A federal Labor MP appears
Federal Labor MP Josh Burns appears to be on the campaign trail today, posting on Instagram he’s there to support MP Nina Taylor.

Josh Frydenberg on the campaign trail

The former federal treasurer Josh Frydenberg is out and about campaigning for the Liberals in Victoria, too, posting “Go Jess!” on X, accompanied by a photo of Frydenberg and some volunteers decked out in blue.
What are the parties promising?

What the heavy rain means for vote-counting
Our political scientist for the election, Luke Mansillo, has sent us this dispatch about what the rain might mean for the election:

double quotation markThe torrential rain in Melbourne has produced a non-insignificant problem for everyone working on the election. Psephologists know that half of the electorate has previously voted ahead of election day and the remaining half of the electorate will vote on election day. These two groups potentially look quite different, so analysts will need to be extra cautious. However, there are going to be fewer people handing out because they do not want to get drenched in the rain; there will be fewer how-to-vote cards that will survive the rain; and, there will be fewer people willing to accept a how-to-vote card as they run into a polling place trying to stay dry. Political parties’ efforts to direct preferences through deals may be less consequential. For these reasons, there will be a systematic bias in the preference flows by 10 to 15% and, when applied to half the electorate, may change the results by about 1% to 3% and possibly higher rates of informality. Thanks to the weather, we will need to wait for the early votes to be reported for many seats.
Key battlegrounds in the Victoria election – video
Our Victorian state correspondent, Benita Kolovos, opens her book of knowledge to get you up to speed on what to look out for as the election results come in.
Meanwhile, the end of group voting tickets means Victoria’s upper house will be looking very different regardless of who wins government.
Voting in person or by postal ballot: what you need to know
More people will be voting in this election than ever before and almost half have already voted. But if you haven’t already voted, here’s what you need to know:
Polling places open from 8am to 6pm on Saturday 28 November. If you’re still in line at 6pm you will still be able to vote.

Legislative council – the upper house – voting has changed. Now voters must number at least five party groups above the line, in order of preference, or at least five individual candidates below the line. Watch our explainer below:
For postal votes, your ballot papers must be sent before 6pm on Saturday 28 November. The Victorian Electoral Commission must receive it by Friday 4 December for it count.

Taylor on the moveJust following the last post, it looks like the federal Liberal leader, Angus Taylor, is getting around today for candidates. The Liberal candidate for South Barwon, Libby Pettit, just posted a photo with Taylor, the Victorian Liberal senator Sarah Henderson and state MP Bev McArthur on Instagram.
A few federal Liberals out and about today it seems.
